before: Score only after collecting enough evidence to explain each rating. Keep unknown distinct from low. An unverified dependency should not receive a neutral score that lets a favored idea rise to the top.
after: Use High when observed evidence supports the rating, Medium when a material dependency remains, and Low when evidence shows a poor fit or a prerequisite is missing. Use Unknown when evidence is absent. Record the facts behind value and readiness separately; do not add the labels into a single score. These labels organize a discussion, not an investment calculation.
rationale: Defines the qualitative screen and keeps missing evidence visible.
evidenceType: author synthesis or fictional teaching data

before: The following results are for candidate HSP-0.8 after the runtime tool set was reduced to request read, approved source search, and pilot draft save. The pilot included 612 eligible units: 318 assisted and 294 comparison. Twelve coordinators participated.
after: All numbers in this packet are invented for practice. Weeks 1-3 used HSP-0.7 for sandbox, shadow, and early assisted work. Its 29 incident-exposed drafts are reported separately below. After a fresh gate, HSP-0.8 froze the model, prompts, source index, freshness checks, permissions, and review interface for weeks 4-6. That cohort contains 612 eligible requests: 318 completed with assistance and 294 in the current workflow. Twelve coordinators participated. Assistance was available on 442 requests; 318 used it and 124 chose fallback. Those 124 are included in the 294 current-workflow requests alongside 170 requests without assistant access. This comparison therefore includes self-selection as well as nonrandom shifts.
rationale: Separates versions and explains overlapping allocation, use, and comparison denominators.
evidenceType: author synthesis or fictional teaching data
